theses.thesis: T1: Free cash flow recovers in 2026, lifting cash generation back above $7 billion.
theses.signpost: FY2026 10-K showing free cash flow above $7.0 billion (filed around February 2027) [1]. Invalidation: FY2026 free cash flow below $6.3 billion or operating cash flow below $7.82 billion.

theses.thesis: T2: Analytical Instruments margin recovers toward 26% as tariff and mix pressure eases.
theses.signpost: FY2026 10-K showing Analytical Instruments segment margin at or above 25% (filed around February 2027). Invalidation: margin below 23% in the FY2026 10-K or a further tariff-driven decline [1].

theses.thesis: T3: Consensus revenue growth of 7.7% in 2026 is delivered and EPS estimates keep rising, but the valuation needs far more growth.
theses.signpost: Q1 2027 results (around April 2027) showing revenue growth of at least 7% and an EPS beat versus consensus [3]. Invalidation: 2026 revenue growth below 5% or a cut in the current-year EPS consensus below $25.28 [3].

theses.thesis: T4: Leverage is manageable, supported by liquidity, but only if returns on capital recover above the 9.5% threshold.
theses.signpost: FY2026 10-K showing total debt at or below $39.4 billion and ROIC above 9.5% [4]. Invalidation: total debt above $41.4 billion without matching earnings growth, or ROIC at or below 8.7% [4].

theses.thesis: T1: Free cash flow recovers in 2026 as the 2025 tax-payment timing reverses, lifting cash generation back above $7 billion.
theses.signpost: FY2026 10-K showing free cash flow above $7.0 billion (filed around February 2027) [1]. Invalidation: FY2026 FCF below $6.3 billion or operating cash flow below $7.82 billion.

theses.thesis: T2: Analytical Instruments margin recovers toward 26% as tariff and mix pressure eases, lifting group segment income.
theses.signpost: FY2026 10-K showing Analytical Instruments segment margin at or above 25% (filed around February 2027). Invalidation: margin below 23% in the FY2026 10-K, or a further tariff-driven margin decline [1].

theses.thesis: T3: Consensus revenue growth of 7.7% in 2026 is delivered and EPS estimates keep rising, but the current valuation needs far more growth than that.
theses.signpost: Q1 2027 results (around April 2027) showing revenue growth of at least 7% and an EPS beat versus consensus [3]. Invalidation: 2026 revenue growth below 5%, or a cut in the current-year EPS consensus below $25.28 [3].

theses.thesis: T4: Leverage is manageable: debt-funded acquisitions and buybacks are supported by strong liquidity, but only if returns on capital recover above 9.5%.
theses.signpost: FY2026 10-K showing total debt at or below $39.4 billion and ROIC above 9.5% [1]. Invalidation: total debt above $41.4 billion without matching earnings growth, or ROIC at or below 8.7% [1][4].
